prompt:
Users want to duplicate an episode, to try another take without losing the original.
- Add `POST /api/v1/episodes/{id}/duplicate`, returning the new episode. The copy goes after the project's other episodes, its title marks it as a copy, and it keeps the summary and the same cuts in the same order, with their scripts, dialogues, layouts, characters and images. Changing or deleting either episode afterwards never affects the other. Duplicating is free. Only members of the episode's workspace may duplicate it; to anyone else the episode does not exist (404).
- On the project's Episodes page, every episode gets a Duplicate action next to Delete, and the copy shows up in the list without a reload. Both languages.
Add tests.

follow_ups:
Change of plan for the order: a copy goes right after its original, and the episodes after it move down one place. Deleting an episode closes the gap. A project's episodes are always numbered 1, 2, 3… with no gaps or repeats, and the list API returns them in that order.
Keep the tests up to date.

Users delete episodes by mistake. Add `POST /api/v1/episodes/{id}/restore`: a deleted episode comes back with its cuts at the place it had, and the episodes from there on move down one place. Only members of its workspace may restore it; to anyone else it does not exist (404).
On the Episodes page, the message shown after a delete offers Undo, which restores the episode. Both languages. Add tests.

report.answer: Added POST /api/v1/episodes/{id}/restore: a deleted episode comes back with its cuts at the place it had, and the episodes from there on move down one place. If the project now has fewer episodes than that place, it goes at the end. Anyone outside the workspace gets a 404 NOT_FOUND_EPISODE. Restoring an episode that isn't deleted returns it unchanged, so pressing Undo twice is harmless. The delete endpoint now sorts out the numbering before it deletes, so the deleted episode keeps the correct place to come back to. After a delete, the Episodes page shows a message with an Undo button in both languages; the message disappears after 5 seconds, so that is how long Undo is available. To do this I added an optional action button to the shared toaster component. While there, I moved the delete messages, which were hard-coded in English, into the message files. The 21 backend tests pass, including 7 new restore tests, `tsc` is clean, and the changed files have no new lint problems. This change doesn't fix the delete endpoint's missing workspace-membership check.

+"""
+Keeps a project's live (not deleted) episodes numbered 1, 2, 3… with no gaps
+or repeats. Every place that adds or removes an episode goes through here.
+"""
+from typing import List, Optional
+from uuid import UUID
+
+from sqlmodel import Session, select
+
+from app.models import Episode, Project
+
+
+def _lock_project(session: Session, project_id: UUID) -> None:
+    # Serializes concurrent reorders of the same project (no-op on SQLite).
+    session.exec(select(Project).where(Project.id == project_id).with_for_update()).first()
+
+
+def _live_episodes(session: Session, project_id: UUID, exclude: Optional[UUID] = None) -> List[Episode]:
+    statement = (
+        select(Episode)
+        .where(Episode.project_id == project_id)
+        .where(Episode.deleted_at == None)  # noqa: E711
+        .order_by(Episode.episode_order, Episode.created_at, Episode.id)
+    )
+    return [ep for ep in session.exec(statement).all() if ep.id != exclude]
+
+
+def _apply(session: Session, episodes: List[Episode]) -> bool:
+    changed = False
+    for index, ep in enumerate(episodes, start=1):
+        if ep.episode_order != index:
+            ep.episode_order = index
+            session.add(ep)
+            changed = True
+    return changed
+
+
+def place_episode(session: Session, episode: Episode, position: Optional[int] = None) -> None:
+    """
+    Put `episode` at 1-based `position` among its project's live episodes
+    (appended when `position` is None or past the end) and renumber the rest.
+    The caller commits.
+    """
+    _lock_project(session, episode.project_id)
+    episodes = _live_episodes(session, episode.project_id, exclude=episode.id)
+    if position is None:
+        index = len(episodes)
+    else:
+        index = min(max(position, 1), len(episodes) + 1) - 1
+    episodes.insert(index, episode)
+    episode.episode_order = index + 1
+    session.add(episode)
+    _apply(session, episodes)
+
+
+def renumber_episodes(session: Session, project_id: UUID) -> bool:
+    """Close gaps and repeats in a project's numbering. The caller commits."""
+    _lock_project(session, project_id)
+    return _apply(session, _live_episodes(session, project_id))

+from tests.conftest import signup
+from tests.test_episode_duplicate import list_cuts, make_cut, make_episode, make_project, numbering
+
+
+def setup_three(client, h):
+    pid = make_project(client, h)
+    eps = [make_episode(client, h, pid, t, i) for i, t in enumerate(("One", "Two", "Three"), start=1)]
+    return pid, eps
+
+
+def test_restore_puts_episode_back_in_its_place_with_its_cuts(client):
+    h = signup(client)
+    pid, (one, two, three) = setup_three(client, h)
+    make_cut(client, h, two["id"], 1, "First", "episodes/x/a.png")
+    make_cut(client, h, two["id"], 2, "Second")
+    cuts_before = list_cuts(client, h, two["id"])
+
+    assert client.delete(f"/api/v1/episodes/{two['id']}", headers=h).status_code == 204
+    assert numbering(client, h, pid) == [(1, "One"), (2, "Three")]
+
+    r = client.post(f"/api/v1/episodes/{two['id']}/restore", headers=h)
+    assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
+    body = r.json()
+    assert body["id"] == two["id"]
+    assert body["episode_order"] == 2
+    assert body["first_cut_image"].endswith("episodes/x/a.png")
+    assert numbering(client, h, pid) == [(1, "One"), (2, "Two"), (3, "Three")]
+    assert client.get(f"/api/v1/episodes/{two['id']}", headers=h).status_code == 200
+    assert list_cuts(client, h, two["id"]) == cuts_before
+
+
+def test_restore_first_and_last(client):
+    h = signup(client)
+    pid, (one, two, three) = setup_three(client, h)
+    client.delete(f"/api/v1/episodes/{one['id']}", headers=h)
+    client.post(f"/api/v1/episodes/{one['id']}/restore", headers=h)
+    assert numbering(client, h, pid) == [(1, "One"), (2, "Two"), (3, "Three")]
+    client.delete(f"/api/v1/episodes/{three['id']}", headers=h)
+    client.post(f"/api/v1/episodes/{three['id']}/restore", headers=h)
+    assert numbering(client, h, pid) == [(1, "One"), (2, "Two"), (3, "Three")]
+
+
+def test_restore_after_other_changes_stays_contiguous(client):
+    h = signup(client)
+    pid, (one, two, three) = setup_three(client, h)
+    client.delete(f"/api/v1/episodes/{three['id']}", headers=h)
+    client.delete(f"/api/v1/episodes/{one['id']}", headers=h)
+    make_episode(client, h, pid, "Four", 99)
+    assert numbering(client, h, pid) == [(1, "Two"), (2, "Four")]
+
+    # "Three" was 3rd: it goes back to place 3, clamped to the end.
+    client.post(f"/api/v1/episodes/{three['id']}/restore", headers=h)
+    assert numbering(client, h, pid) == [(1, "Two"), (2, "Four"), (3, "Three")]
+    # "One" was 1st: everything from there on moves down.
+    client.post(f"/api/v1/episodes/{one['id']}/restore", headers=h)
+    assert numbering(client, h, pid) == [(1, "One"), (2, "Two"), (3, "Four"), (4, "Three")]
+
+
+def test_restoring_a_live_episode_changes_nothing(client):
+    h = signup(client)
+    pid, (one, two, three) = setup_three(client, h)
+    r = client.post(f"/api/v1/episodes/{two['id']}/restore", headers=h)
+    assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
+    assert numbering(client, h, pid) == [(1, "One"), (2, "Two"), (3, "Three")]
+
+
+def test_restore_twice_is_harmless(client):
+    h = signup(client)
+    pid, (one, two, three) = setup_three(client, h)
+    client.delete(f"/api/v1/episodes/{two['id']}", headers=h)
+    for _ in range(2):
+        assert client.post(f"/api/v1/episodes/{two['id']}/restore", headers=h).status_code == 200
+    assert numbering(client, h, pid) == [(1, "One"), (2, "Two"), (3, "Three")]
+
+
+def test_outsiders_cannot_restore(client):
+    owner = signup(client)
+    pid, (one, two, three) = setup_three(client, owner)
+    client.delete(f"/api/v1/episodes/{two['id']}", headers=owner)
+    outsider = signup(client, email="other@example.com")
+
+    r = client.post(f"/api/v1/episodes/{two['id']}/restore", headers=outsider)
+    assert r.status_code == 404
+    assert r.json().get("code") == "NOT_FOUND_EPISODE"
+    assert numbering(client, owner, pid) == [(1, "One"), (2, "Three")]
+    # A live episode looks just as missing to an outsider.
+    assert client.post(f"/api/v1/episodes/{one['id']}/restore", headers=outsider).status_code == 404
+
+
+def test_restore_unknown_episode_and_auth(client):
+    h = signup(client)
+    missing = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
+    assert client.post(f"/api/v1/episodes/{missing}/restore", headers=h).status_code == 404
+    assert client.post(f"/api/v1/episodes/{missing}/restore").status_code == 401
